name: EPF
seoDesc: EPF: work out employee contribution from the basic pay and the dearness allowance. A free finance calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The EPF calculator turns the basic pay, the dearness allowance and more into employee contribution. That makes it useful for a budget, a loan conversation, a payslip check or a what-if before you talk to a lender. The formula is printed further down, so you can check the answer by hand if you want to.

sections.title: How does the EPF calculator work?
sections.html:
The EPF calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports employee contribution in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the basic pay, the dearness allowance, the employee contribution percent and the present age.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

sections.title: The formula behind the EPF calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Employee contribution=((1 ÷ 100) × employee contribution percent × (basic pay + dearness allowance))
Employer contribution=(basic pay + dearness allowance − 15000, ((1 ÷ 100) × employer contribution percent × (basic pay + dearness allowance)) + ((833 ÷ 10000) × basic pay + (833 ÷ 10000) × dearness allowance − 2499 ÷ 2), ((1 ÷ 100) × employer contribution percent × (basic pay + dearness allowance)))
Employer contribution main=((1 ÷ 100) × employer contribution percent × (basic pay + dearness allowance))
Employer contribution eps excess=((833 ÷ 10000) × basic pay + (833 ÷ 10000) × dearness allowance − 2499 ÷ 2)
EPF maturity amount=(basic pay, dearness allowance, employee contribution percent, employer contribution percent, present age, retirement age, current EPF balance, expected salary hike rate, EPF interest rate)
Total employee contribution=(basic pay, dearness allowance, employee contribution percent, present age, retirement age, current EPF balance, expected salary hike rate)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Time, opening in months

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The EPF calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Comparing two offers that quote their costs in different ways
  • Building a monthly budget and testing how one number shifts the rest
  • Sizing up a purchase before you commit to it
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the basic pay, the dearness allowance and the employee contribution percent — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html: • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the EPF calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns employee contribution, derived from the basic pay, the dearness allowance and the employee contribution percent. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the EPF calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the basic pay, the dearness allowance, the employee contribution percent and the present age, which is 9 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter basic pay in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Basic pay opens in months and the chip beside it offers 27 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.

faq.q: Is the EPF calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. The calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
